Definition: from G5368; friendly; Philemon, a Christian:--Philemon.
BiblicalUsage: Philemon is a Christian of Colossae, the master of the runaway slave Onesimus, and Paul writes him the shortest letter in the New Testament. The letter calls him dearly beloved and fellowlabourer, and Paul asks him to receive Onesimus back, no longer as a servant but as a brother beloved.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Philemon's name is remembered because a letter about forgiveness was written to him: the gospel made a master and a slave into brothers, and Paul trusted him to live it.
